title: From Failure to Success How We Transformed Our Assessment Strategy https://www.teachwire.net/news/from-failure-to-success-how-we-transformed-our-assessment-strategy
author: Ben Rice
summary: Ben Rice describes a systematic, comprehensive transformation of assessment practices that moved from ineffective testing protocols to assessment genuinely useful for instructional decision-making. Initial assessment strategies failed to provide actionable information about student learning and instead consumed valuable instructional time without improving teaching. The transformation involved fundamentally rethinking what assessments should measure, how frequently to assess, and how to use assessment data to improve teaching decisions. The resulting system provides teachers with real-time information about student understanding without excessive testing burden or administrative overhead. This case study demonstrates that assessment improvement isn't about adding more tests or increasing testing frequency, but rather fundamentally rethinking assessment purpose and design to ensure alignment with instructional goals. The work illustrates principles applicable across different schools, contexts, and instructional settings.
points: Ineffective assessment consumes instructional time without improving teaching decisions or student outcomes
Assessment system redesign begins with clarifying purpose: what will we do with this information?
Frequent poorly-designed assessments provide noise rather than signal about actual student learning
Sustainable assessment systems balance information gathering with preservation of instructional efficiency
Assessment transformation requires questioning fundamental assumptions about what and how to measure learning
quotes: From failure to success in assessment means rethinking what assessments are actually for.
Bad assessment strategies feel productive because they generate lots of data, but the data is useless.
The goal isn't more testing. The goal is testing that makes teaching better.
Assessment redesign starts with asking: What will we actually do with this information?
